This cohort does not constrain the span kind, so a SERVER or INTERNAL span carrying the same HTTP attributes can satisfy the client contract. The HTTP classifier only omits such a span from client coverage; it does not make this exact expectation fail. Require `CLIENT` here and in every cohort so the shared oracle actually validates client spans.

replies.body:
Addressed in 4cbcddef14fbf837ac0382d8cc1165f6ea09bb16.

Analysis: Each shared HTTP cohort selected spans only by method and response status. Adding `kind: CLIENT` to every match makes the expectations reject server and internal spans with the same attributes.

Upsides: The shared contract now checks the intended span type for every response cohort and cannot pass against unrelated spans.

Downsides: The contract now rejects telemetry that omits or misreports the client span kind. That stricter result is intended.

threads.body: `ObjectMapper.readTree` returns `null` for an empty or whitespace-only response, so calling `.equals` on the actual node throws `NullPointerException` rather than reporting a contract validation failure. Compare from the known-valid expected node (or explicitly handle a null actual node) so blank server responses fail cleanly.

replies.body:
Addressed in 9dea068a47f1a4e4c861ba9641e3d7d5c0a09404.

Analysis: The contract renders a known-valid expected JSON body. Using that node as the equality receiver lets an empty response parse to null and compare unequal instead of throwing NullPointerException.

Upsides: Blank responses now produce the same clear contract validation failure as other mismatched JSON bodies. The regression test covers this edge case.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: The declaration check happens after `json.loads`, so a truncated or otherwise malformed stale report for a deleted scenario still aborts reduction with `JSONDecodeError` instead of being ignored. Filter by `path.stem` before opening/parsing the file so undeclared reports are truly excluded.

Addressed in 55983b34ecc81c5a9e8ce2e9f4d06cf5022abb3c.

Analysis: The scenario name is available from the report filename without reading its contents. Checking the package specification first ensures that every undeclared report is skipped before JSON parsing.

Upsides: Stale malformed reports for deleted scenarios no longer abort coverage reduction. The existing undeclared-report test now covers both valid and truncated stale files.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: `npm ci` requires a lockfile (typically `package-lock.json`) in `tools/http/test-client/js`. Since this PR introduces a new dependency there, ensure the corresponding lockfile is added/updated so CI doesn’t fail at install time (or switch to `npm install` if the repo intentionally doesn’t commit lockfiles).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: `tools/http/test-client/js/package-lock.json` is committed for the helper package. The workspace lockfile at `scenarios/http/js/package-lock.json` is also committed and records the helper's `yaml` dependency. `npm ci --prefix scenarios/http/js` completes without changing either lockfile.

Upsides: CI keeps deterministic installs through the existing lockfiles. No package-manager behavior needs to change.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: Reduction reads reports recursively (`_report.py:150`), but this cleanup only scans one nested level. A stale `old/unrelated/inference.json` therefore survives and is treated as the current declared `inference` scenario, allowing old samples and findings to contaminate the newly reduced data. Remove matching report names at every nested depth while preserving the freshly written root-level reports, and update the new test that currently expects the deep duplicate to survive.
